name: Rat
description: Hippocampal place cells fire at specific locations creating cognitive maps. Grid cells in entorhinal cortex tile space with hexagonal firing patterns. Sleep replay compresses hours of exploration into seconds for memory consolidation.

core_attributes.neurology: hippocampal place cells, entorhinal grid cells, prefrontal replay circuits
core_attributes.pattern: cognitive spatial mapping, hexagonal grid cells, sleep replay consolidation

scope.definition: Spatial navigation accuracy of rats using place cells — proportion of correct maze path choices based on internal cognitive map without external sensory cues, after cue removal in probe trials.

evidence.source: O'Keefe & Nadel (1978) 'The Hippocampus as a Cognitive Map', Oxford UP; Morris et al. (1982) 'Place navigation impaired in rats with hippocampal lesions', Nature 297:681-683.
cross_domain_examples: hippocampus-lesioned rats fail water maze navigation — confirms cognitive map as hippocampus-dependent
place cell firing encodes 2D position with 15-30 cm spatial resolution in open fields
grid cells (entorhinal cortex) provide metric coordinate system — 2005 Nobel Prize supporting evidence
dead-reckoning in desert ants: path integration with analogous internal spatial representation

scope.falsifiability: If hippocampal lesions leave spatial navigation unimpaired, the cognitive map is not localized to hippocampus and a different implementation exists.
scope.measurement_limits: Cognitive map accuracy degrades over multi-day intervals without re-exposure. Novel environments require 20-30 minutes of exploration before stable place field maps form. Map resolution decreases in large environments.

scope.definition: Regularity of grid cell firing pattern — R² of hexagonal lattice fit to autocorrelogram of grid cell spatial firing in open field exploration.

evidence.source: Hafting et al. (2005) 'Microstructure of a spatial map in the entorhinal cortex', Nature 436:801-806; Moser et al. (2008) 'Place cells, grid cells, and the brain's spatial representation system', Annual Review of Neuroscience.
cross_domain_examples: entorhinal grid cells: hexagonal firing fields tiling space with R²=0.92-0.96 — near-perfect periodicity
grid cell spacing increases 3× between dorsal-ventral entorhinal axis — multi-scale metric representation
path integration robots using grid-cell-inspired algorithms: 0.88 spatial accuracy in GPS-denied navigation

scope.falsifiability: If grid cell firing patterns are found to be non-hexagonal (irregular or square) across multiple species and environments, the hexagonal lattice metric is not a universal spatial coding scheme.
scope.measurement_limits: Hexagonality is not perfect in all environments — wall geometry can distort grid pattern. Grid cells are also found in bats, humans (fMRI), and monkeys — cross-species validation strengthens universality.

scope.definition: Correlation between hippocampal place cell firing sequences during awake navigation and subsequent slow-wave sleep replay — measured as template-match correlation coefficient of firing order.

evidence.source: Wilson & McNaughton (1994) 'Reactivation of hippocampal ensemble memories during sleep', Science 265:676-679; Nádasdy et al. (1999) 'Replay and time compression of recurring spike sequences in the hippocampus', Journal of Neuroscience 19:9497.
cross_domain_examples: post-navigation sleep replay: firing sequence correlation 0.87 vs 0.12 chance; time-compressed 6-20×
reverse replay during awake immobility suggests planning function — prospective coding evidence
human hippocampal replay: fMRI pattern reactivation during sleep matches learning session activity

scope.falsifiability: If sleep hippocampal sequences are uncorrelated with prior navigation sequences (R² <0.20), the memory consolidation replay hypothesis fails.
scope.measurement_limits: Replay detection requires multi-unit recording during REM and NREM sleep following specific navigation tasks. The correlation is calculated on firing sequences, not individual cell rates — noise-sensitive analysis.
